notes.meaning: While Jesus was teaching in the synagogue on the Sabbath, a demon-possessed man shouted out. The evil spirit had taken control of the man and could not stand being in the presence of Jesus. The demon is called unclean because it is evil, opposes God's Holy Spirit, and defiles human lives.

The demon spoke through the man, showing terror at Jesus. It recognized Jesus of Nazareth as the Messiah, calling Him the Holy One of God. Even though the evil spirit knew who Jesus was, it hated Him and knew that He had come to destroy the power of Satan.

Jesus ordered the evil spirit to be silent and come out of the man. The word for be silent literally means to be muzzled. Jesus refused to receive praise or testimony from a demon, showing His complete authority over evil powers.

The evil spirit had to obey Jesus, but it threw the man into violent shaking and let out a loud screech as it left. Because Satan is cruel, he tried to do as much harm as possible on the way out. Yet the man was delivered from the demon's grasp and completely freed.

The people in the synagogue were filled with wonder at what they had witnessed. They noticed that Jesus taught with direct authority rather than quoting other teachers, and that even foul spirits obeyed His command. His miracles proved that His message truly came from God.

Reports about this astonishing miracle quickly spread all over the surrounding region of Galilee. People told their neighbors how Jesus had taught and cast out the demon by His own command. This widespread report prepared crowds of people to hear Him wherever He went.

After leaving the synagogue service, Jesus went directly to the house where Simon Peter and Andrew lived. He brought James and John along with Him. Even after doing public miracles, Jesus cared for the personal needs of His close followers and their families.

Simon Peter's mother-in-law was lying in bed suffering from a severe fever. As soon as Jesus entered, the family told Him about her condition, trusting in His kindness and power. They knew the One who drove out spirits could also heal bodily illness.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some Catholic interpreters suggest Peter may have been a widower since his wife is not mentioned at the bedside, and the Church views priestly celibacy as a disciplinary practice rather than an unchangeable dogma.

notes.meaning: Jesus walked over to the sick woman, took her hand, and helped her up. The fever left her body instantly, and she felt strong enough to prepare and serve a meal for them. Her immediate service showed both that her cure was complete and that her heart was full of thanks.

Once the sun set, the Sabbath day was officially over, and the people felt free to carry their sick without breaking Sabbath customs. They brought crowds of sick and demon-oppressed people directly to Jesus. He welcomed them and showed deep pity for their misery.

Almost the whole town crowded outside the doorway of Peter's house to see Jesus. People gathered both to seek healing for themselves and to watch His amazing works. The doorway became like a public clinic where the Savior met human suffering face-to-face.

Jesus healed many people who had all kinds of sicknesses and drove out many demons. He refused to let the demons speak because they knew He was the Christ. Jesus would not allow wicked spirits to serve as preachers of His holy name.

Very early the next morning, while it was still dark, Jesus slipped out of the house into a quiet, lonely place to pray. Even though He was busy doing good, He made time to be alone with His Heavenly Father. His practice shows how important secret prayer is for spiritual strength.

Simon Peter and the other disciples woke up, saw that Jesus was missing, and urgently searched for Him. They tracked Him down until they found the quiet spot where He was praying. Peter wanted Jesus to return to the town and continue His popular ministry there.

When the disciples found Jesus, they urged Him to come back, telling Him that everyone was looking for Him. They were excited by His sudden popularity and wanted Him to meet the waiting crowds. Yet Jesus was not driven by human praise or public excitement.

Jesus replied that they needed to move on to the neighboring country towns so He could preach there too. He explained that proclaiming God's message was the very reason He came out from the Father into the world. He would not let the popularity of one city keep Him from reaching others.

Jesus traveled throughout the entire region of Galilee, teaching the truth in the Jewish synagogues and casting out evil spirits. His miracles confirmed the holy message He proclaimed. By delivering captives from Satan, He showed that God's kingdom had truly arrived.

A man with leprosy came and fell on his knees before Jesus, pleading to be made clean. Leprosy was a dreaded skin condition that cut a person off from society and temple worship. The man did not question Jesus' power to heal him; he only submitted humbly to Jesus' will.

differ.view: Some teach that God always wills physical healing for believers, so praying 'if you are willing' is unnecessary.
Many evangelicals teach that the leper's humble submission shows that bodily healing rests on God's sovereign choice rather than an automatic guarantee.

notes.meaning: Filled with tender pity, Jesus reached out and touched the man who had long been isolated from human contact. By law, touching a leper made someone ceremonially unclean, but Jesus' touch brought pure healing instead of taking on defilement. He spoke with divine authority, saying, 'I am willing; be clean!'

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: A few ancient manuscripts read that Jesus was moved with anger rather than compassion, though most scholars and ancient copies support pity.

notes.meaning: The moment Jesus spoke the command, the terrible disease left the man completely. His skin was made whole and pure without any lingering trace of illness. This instant cure proved the mighty power of Christ's word over disease.

Jesus immediately sent the man away with a strict, forceful warning. The strong language shows the earnest importance Jesus placed on His instructions. He wanted the man to follow God's law promptly and avoid unnecessary public stir.

Jesus ordered the man not to talk to anyone, but to go straight to the priest and offer the sacrifices required by Moses. Having the priest inspect him would officially certify that he was clean and restore him to the community. It also served as a clear proof to the priests that God was at work through Jesus.

Instead of staying quiet, the overjoyed man widely spread the news of his wonderful cure. Because of the enormous crowds that rushed to see Him, Jesus could no longer enter the towns openly. He stayed out in remote, deserted areas, yet people kept streaming to Him from all directions.
